intent: Switch to the previous page of a paged result set through state, with a chevron and a short label.
typical_uses: The previous button at the start of the page row, disabled at the first page
Half of a previous/next pair with no page numbers

dont_use_when.situation: A button to one numbered page
A button to the next page
A link to the previous page, where each page has its own URL

invariants.text: The button renders a left chevron before the label and ignores children. Its accessible name is the fixed `aria-label` "Go to previous page", set ahead of the consumer's props: `text` changes only the visible label, and only an `aria-label` passed to it replaces the name.
The visible label is hidden below a 640px viewport width (pagination.module.css `.previousNextText`), so a narrow viewport shows the chevron alone.
The chevron is mirrored under a right-to-left direction (pagination.module.css `.chevron:dir(rtl)`), so it keeps pointing toward the previous pages whatever the reading direction.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass a matching `aria-label` with a custom `text`, so the visible label stays part of the accessible name

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Go to previous page' }) finds the button, with the visible "Previous" label and an svg inside it, and that it is disabled when asked

rtl.by: pagination.module.css mirrors the chevron with `.chevron:dir(rtl)` and pagination.test.tsx pins that rule, but jsdom has no layout and does not resolve `:dir()`, so no suite renders the button right-to-left

unexposed_parts.reason: pagination.tsx renders a ChevronLeftIcon inside the button; it is not exported as a component of its own and cannot be replaced.
pagination.tsx renders `text` in a span with the stylesheet's previousNextText class; it is not exported, and `text` is the only control over it.

bad.title: A label given as children
bad.why: The button renders fixed content and ignores children; the visible label is set through `text`.
